subject: Creativity
title: The Innovator's Dilemma: Why Success Breeds Failure
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Innovator's Dilemma: Why Success Breeds Failure.

hook.text: Kodak invented the digital camera in 1975 — then buried it to protect film profits. They filed for bankruptcy in 2012.

buildup.text: The Innovator's Dilemma: successful companies can't adopt disruptive innovations because doing so would cannibalize.

discovery.text: Kodak's rational choice was to protect film. Film was 70% margin. Digital was 5%.

twist.text: Nokia, Blackberry, Blockbuster, and Sears all made the same rational mistake.

climax.text: The solution: create separate units for disruptive innovation with different metrics, leadership, and culture.

punchline.text: The safest choice is often the most dangerous one. Just ask Kodak.

quiz.question: Why did Kodak suppress its own digital camera invention?
options: Protecting profitable film business (70% margins vs 5% digital)

details.summary: The innovator's dilemma describes how successful companies fail by doing everything right. Listening to current customers, investing in profitable products, and optimizing existing processes all make companies vulnerable to disruption from below because they rationally ignore low-margin innovations.
details.whyItMatters: The dilemma reveals that good management can lead to failure in the face of disruptive change. It is one of the most important strategic concepts for leaders navigating technological transitions.
takeaways: Serving current customers well can blind companies to disruptive threats
Rational resource allocation favors existing markets over emerging ones
Companies must invest in disruption even when it threatens current products

faq.question: How does doing everything right lead to failure?
faq.answer: Companies listen to their best customers who want incremental improvements. They invest in the highest-margin products. These rational decisions cause them to ignore small, low-margin innovations that eventually improve to capture the entire market.

faq.question: What companies have fallen to the innovator's dilemma?
faq.answer: Kodak with digital photography, Blockbuster with Netflix, Nokia with smartphones, and traditional taxis with ride-sharing all followed the classic pattern. Each was dominant and well-managed but failed to adapt to disruptive innovation from below.
